subject: SSQ: PII handling — tokenization options and cross-border routing
messages:
From: Anna Zhu <anna.zhu@wellpointanalytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@wellpointanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SSQ: tokenization & cross-border routing (initial questionnaire)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking the time to engage on our privacy/security questionnaire. Attached is a short SSQ focused on PII handling, data classification, and cross-border routing for our planned pilot. A few items are highest priority for Wellpoint:

- Clarification on whether Redwood can provide per-tenant tokenization (or pseudonymization) at ingestion.
- If tokenization is supported, does the KMS key reside in the customer tenant? Can we bring our own key (BYOK)?
- Dataflow: will raw PII ever leave the customer VPC/region (we need a diagram that shows routing and subprocessors)?
- Subprocessor list & whether Redwood uses any third-party data processors that will touch content or metadata.
- Which transfer mechanisms do you rely on for EU->US routing (SCCs, adequacy, or other)?

Would you be able to share a short (1-2 page) dataflow diagram and answers to the above by COB Monday? Legal is looped on this email.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Zhu
Head of Security Operations
Wellpoint Analytics

Attachment: Wellpoint_SSQ.pdf (3 pages - highlighted questions)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Anna Zhu <anna.zhu@wellpointanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SSQ: tokenization & cross-border routing (initial questionnaire)

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary answers below; I attached a short one-page dataflow PNG and a draft SSQ response PDF (see attachments).

- Per-tenant tokenization: Redwood supports tokenization at the ingestion layer via an optional transform. We offer both service-side tokenization and a BYOK tokenization mode where the customer manages KMS keys (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via standard APIs).
- BYOK/KMS: In BYOK mode the keys never leave the customer project; Redwood holds encrypted key references and uses envelope encryption. We can provide KMS attestation info and our key usage policy in the security package.
- Dataflow & cross-border: For Hosted API, we route requests to the nearest region by default but can enforce regional pinning to keep raw PII within a specific region. When regional pinning is enabled, we do not route raw PII outside the selected region; only aggregated telemetry/metrics (no raw tokens) are forwarded for system health. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can opt for VPC-only patterns — raw payloads stay in-customer. The attached dataflow diagram shows routing and subprocessors.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessor list and have a Notice/Approval process for adding subprocessors. Current subprocessors relevant to data movement are listed in the PDF.
- Transfers: We support SCCs (standard contractual clauses) for EU->US transfers and rely on a documented legal basis per customer contract. For regulated customers wanting additional controls we offer Private deployment or Dedicated capacity in EU regions.

I'm copying Monica and Rishi for technical and legal follow-ups. Happy to walk through the diagram on Monday.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_data_map_v2.png, Wellpoint_SSQ_Responses_v1.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SSQ: tokenization & cross-border routing (follow-up & technical detail)

Hi Anna,

Following up with a bit more technical detail and a proposed configuration for your pilot. Highlights:

- Tokenization flow (service-side): We accept the raw payload over TLS, perform tokenization in a dedicated worker pool, store token mappings in an encrypted vault (optionally customer-owned), and pass tokenized content to the inference runtime. The runtime never receives the original PII in tokenized mode.
- BYOK flow: If you choose BYOK for token encryption, keys live in your KMS and Redwood only stores encrypted tokens under customer-specific key references. We rotate envelope keys quarterly by default; customer-managed rotation schedules are supported via policy.
- Metadata handling: We treat routing metadata (IP geolocation, region tag) as operational metadata and can suppress or redact it from telemetry for privacy-sensitive customers.
- Subprocessor specifics: Third-party observability (metrics) vendors are only used for anonymized metrics; we do not send message content to those vendors. The PDF lists the vendor names and their minimal data footprint.
- Evidence: Attached is a copy of our KMS integration guide and a short SCC template excerpt; Legal can take the SCC excerpt and adapt as needed.

If you want, we can prepare a one-page mutual action plan: pilot scope, success criteria (latency, PII-at-rest metrics), and minimal compliance artifacts to share with your auditors. Would next Wednesday at 10am ET work for a 30-minute technical sync?

Cheers,
Monica
Monica Patel
Product Security Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_kms_guide.pdf, scc_excerpt.docx
